To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DIRAC Data Management has been improved in order to guarantee the integrity, consistency and coherence of data, and the DIRAC Storage Usage Agent has been developed and is being used in production.
the DIRAC Data Management system has been improved by the introduction of a new Storage Usage agent, a new Bookkeeping database and a new Bookkeeping interface to DIRAC.

1) the LHCb data management system is able to maintain a coherent and consistent picture of data, 2) the DMS is able to detect and cure data corruption, missing files and inconsistencies in the data management system, and 3) the DIRAC DMS is able, in a generic manner, to detect and correct data management problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated system for data consistency, integrity and storage usage monitoring.
the following topics: * Bookkeeping database: data consistency and integrity checks * LFC mirror database: storage usage agent * LCG File Catalogues (LFC): data consistency and integrity check

the development of an efficient and robust data management system, capable of dealing with the complexity of a large scale distributed system such as the LHCb computing grid, and the large amount of data that is produced by the experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DIRAC Data Management has been successfully tested in all its components.
the DIRAC DMS is now able to cope with all the issues that may affect data management and data integrity, and that the DMS is now in a stable and robust condition.
the LHCb DMS is a complex, but stable and robust system, able to cope with the large amount of data generated by the LHCb experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed tools for the analysis and monitoring of data integrity and consistency, tools for the analysis of the data usage and tools for the analysis for the Bookkeeping data.
we have achieved a coherent and consistent view of the DIRAC data management system.
the LHCb DMS has reached a level of robustness and stability that allows the LHCb collaboration to perform its physics analysis without any concern about missing or corrupted data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DIRAC Data Management can be considered as a reliable and stable tool to handle the LHCb data.
a systematic approach to data quality control is essential in the context of a complex and evolving distributed computing environment.

the LHCb Bookkeeping database can be used as a central point of reference for all the data stored on the WLCG infrastructure, and it can be used to monitor and check the consistency of all the other WLCG components (LFC, Storage Elements, etc.)
